author: trevorld
body:
* Character values are now passed as "raw" strings to Python

  + In particular this avoids triggering an error in Python 3.12 when creating a string with escapes not supported by Python e.g. `default = "\\D"` will continue to return a default value of `"\\D"` instead of triggering an error.
  + However, this also means that any Python accepted escape sequences will no longer be interpreted as an escape sequence. If relying on such behaviour you may need to instead use the appropriate R escape sequences or Unicode values instead of Python escape sequences:

    - E.g. `default = "\\t"` will now return a default value of `"\\t"` (a `t` preceded by an (escaped) backslash) instead of `"\t"` (a horizontal tab).
    - https://docs.python.org/3/reference/lexical_analysis.html#escape-sequences
    - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basic_Latin_(Unicode_block)

  + Thanks Matthew Hall (@mdhall272) for bug report.

closes #51

body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack) (oldest at bottom):
* #123077
* __->__ #123484

Debugging is happening in https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/123126 . 

Upgrading triton cause accuracy failure for mixer_b16_224  and levit_128 . 

mixer_b16_224 is debugged specifically. It due to extra FMA instructions being used in a single kernel. That kernel itself only introduce small numerical difference. We conclude that this is not some 'real' accuracy issue and we should raise the tolerance to unblock the triton pin update.

The tolerance is picked such that the CI accuracy test can pass.

author: jastornig
body:
Changes: Main activity allows for switching between activities that work on their own, but not yet together.

Connection activity: This activity allows the user to browse for games, select one and connect to it. A new game can also be created. 

For demonstration purposes, a connection to the stomp broker is established with the obtained token. The user will see a Toast if a new player connects to the game where he is connected to. 

Currently there is no visual feedback that a user is indeed connected to a game despite a Toast that is shown once a connection has been established. Error handling needs to be improved.

The connected game (or its descriptors as well as the token) should be stored in a local datastore so that the user can reconnect to the game in case of connection loss.

author: mistermoe
body:
# Summary
This PR is another iteration in our binary search towards finding the right package structure. Initial structure was too nested. 2nd iteration is far too flat and a bit unwieldy with 18,473 `With*` option functions (keenly pointed out by @phoebe-lew)

![image](https://github.com/TBD54566975/tbdex-go/assets/4887440/844d9e88-32db-4914-88ce-e40a30134438)

# Changes
put offerings related stuff into an `offerings` package. we can follow suit for each resource and message type. Generalized stuff like `Message`, `Resource`, `Sign`, `Verify` can stay in the `tbdex` package. 

Name collisions for consumers can be handled if relevant by aliasing the import e.g. 
```go
import tbdexoffering "github.com/TBD54566975/tbdex-go/tbdex/offering"
```

---

Refactored offering creation and removed 100+ lines of duplicated code. `Offering` is the chonkiest resource in tbDEX and creating one with endless `With*` Options was really hard to do. Switched over to something a bit simpler.

The refactor allows offerings to be created in several ways using the same underlying code:

#### Split out
incase the payin and payout fields are huge

```go
usdWirePayin := offering.NewPayin("USD", []offering.PayinMethod{
    offering.NewPayinMethod("WIRE"),
})

usdStoredBalancePayout := offering.NewPayout("USDC", []offering.PayoutMethod{
    offering.NewPayoutMethod("STORED_BALANCE", 20*time.Minute),
})

offering.Create(usdWirePayin, usdStoredBalancePayout, "1.0")
```

#### YOLO Structs
```go
offering.Create(
    offering.PayinDetails{
        CurrencyCode: "USD",
        Methods:      []offering.PayinMethod{
            offering.NewPayinMethod("WIRE"),
            offering.NewPayinMethod("SQUAREPAY"),
        },
    },
    offering.PayoutDetails{
        CurrencyCode: "USDC",
        Methods:      []offering.PayoutMethod{
            offering.NewPayoutMethod("STORED_BALANCE", 20*time.Minute),
        },
    },
    "1",
    offering.RequiredClaims(pexv2.PresentationDefinition{}),
)
```

---

Added Missing `RequiredClaims` field to `Offering`

> [!IMPORTANT]
> [RequiredClaims](https://github.com/TBD54566975/tbdex-go/blob/refactor/tbdex/offering/offering.go#L31) is a pointer to `pexv2.PresentationDefinition` in order to prevent marshaling/unmarshaling from setting it to its zero-state. Ideally would use @alecthomas 's [`optional.Option`](https://github.com/alecthomas/types/blob/master/optional/option.go) but it marshals to `null` for `nil` pointers which borks what the json schema expects. not necessarily happy with using a pointer but couldn't think of a better solution atm.


---

Added strongly typed representation for [OfferingID](https://github.com/TBD54566975/tbdex-go/blob/refactor/tbdex/offering/offering.go#L75-L81)

## Description

Multiple refinements to tag drawer: https://github.com/openedx/modular-learning/issues/190

- Read mode and edit mode of the drawer.
- Global state to revert changes made in edit mode.
- Save all changes on edit model when user clicks on `Save`.
- New styles.

## Supporting information

- Github issue: https://github.com/openedx/modular-learning/issues/190
- Related PRs:
    - https://github.com/openedx/edx-platform/pull/34490
    - https://github.com/openedx/openedx-learning/pull/180
- Internal ticket: [FAL-3645](https://tasks.opencraft.com/browse/FAL-3645)

## Testing instructions

- Use this branch of edx-platform: https://github.com/openedx/edx-platform/pull/34490
- Run `make requirements` on cms shell.
- Make sure you have some sample taxonomy/tags data setup: https://github.com/open-craft/taxonomy-sample-data
- Go into a course and click on "Manage tags" option for any unit/block
- Confirm:
    - Taxonomies with tags added to them are open by default, and ordered according to the number of tags they contain
    - Taxonomies with no tags are listed alphabetically below the taxonomies with tags
    - A footer with actions has been added to the drawer. In read-only mode it displays "Close" and "Edit Tags".
    - The new style of tags tree.
    - You are on read only mode: You can't add/remove tags.
    - You can close the drawer with the "Close" button
- Click on "Edit tags" and confirm:
    - X's appear next to deletable tags
    - Any collapsed taxonomies expand
    - "Add a tag" fields (https://github.com/openedx/modular-learning/issues/188) appear at the bottom of the sections for each taxonomy
    - Buttons in the footer change to "cancel" and "save"
    - Make sure the drawer scrolls
- Add and delete tags for any taxonomy
- Click on Cancel and verify that the drawer changes to read mode and all your changes are canceled.
- Click on "Edit tags" and add/delete tags and click "Save" and verify.
    - Your changes are saved.
    - The drawer changes to Read-Only mode but stays open
    - A toast appears in the bottom left of the page saying "N tags added", "N tags removed", or "X tags added, Y tags removed"
- Test the different states of the toast:
    - Add and remove tags.
    - Only add tags.
    - Only remove tags.

author: laholstege
body:
1) we have a AI and UI state. the AI is created at the bottom of `actions.tsx` and provided on the client like context on `app/page.tsx` 2) we don't need to pass around many props, we do `useUIState` on the client to add to the state. we use a server action `submitUserMessage` instead of an `onSubmit`. 3) submitUserMessage is where the magic happens. we start streaming a UI for the entire array of ReactNodes for the messages. so first we add the user's message, then the empty bot message 4) we start the async process to generate the initial system message and stream updates 5) we actually start running the LLM and stream that text back, then close out all the streams 6) on `main.tsx` the UI itself is rendered as this because it is just an array of nodes ``` {messagesUI .map((m) => {return
{m.display}
;})} ``` --- things i'm not sure about: 1) why session is fetched multiple times. my thought is that each page should check auth on the server before even calling the db, so i don't check auth() again on `getChat` or `getChatHistory`. i feel like this shouldn't matter since we're just doing the historyService call from the server..? 2) why it takes a second to load the 👍 👎 on feedback when you refresh the page. the UCD logo also flickers, and homepage policybot svg. also why the first load is so massive?? i get layout.js at 2.1 MB and page.js at 2.0 MB. if i comment out the font awesome icons/imports that goes down to 642 kB and 1.0 MB 3) we could show the message on the sidebar before it is completed (and an animation to make it look like it's typing) if we save the system (and possibly user) message to the db immediately, so when we do `router.refresh()` and the sidebar calls `getChats()` it will pull that one 4) better way to reset chat than going to `/` which redirects to `/chat/new` when clicking "ask a new question" 5) best pattern for error handling? i've done it on `page.tsx` so it handles not found or not authorized. but should those be errors thrown by the db? also i stopped using `Suspense` because the only real loading state we have is handled by the streamableUI. 6) it's not super clear when it is unsafe to use data without sanitizing it. like, i'm calling `saveChat()` from actions.tsx (which is a server component)–could i just pass in the entire object? would it be safe to save the `llmModel` from that object? and i need @cydoval to look at the animations and also make the side history scrollable ## Summary by CodeRabbit - **New Features** - Introduced animation effects for chat history. - Added a new `NotFound` component to display a 404 error message. - Added a `NotAuthorized` component for access restriction scenarios. - Implemented new chat box form for user interactions. - Enhanced chat application with `newChatSession` logic for better session management. - **Enhancements** - Improved layout and presentation of the About page. - Updated chat components for better performance and user experience. - Reorganized chat service code for OpenAI integration. - **Bug Fixes** - Fixed attribute naming conventions in SVG components. - **Documentation** - Added necessary import statements across various components for clarity. - **Style** - Added and updated styling for the chat history section. - **Refactor** - Streamlined code and logic across chat components and services. - **Dependencies** - Added `"framer-motion"` to enhance UI with motion effects.

author: reactorscram
body:
Fixes #4488 

```[tasklist]
# Before merging
- [x] There's one call site that won't compile on Linux. Make this cross-platform.
- [x] Does the rule get removed every time when you quit gracefully?
- [x] Will this NRPT rule prevent connlib from re-resolving the portal IP if it needs to?
- [x] Test network switching. Does this work worse, better, or the same?
- [ ] Is the Windows DNS cache flushed exactly when it needs to be?
```

- After connlib connects to the portal, we add an NRPT rule asking Windows to send **all** DNS queries to our sentinels. This should also be called whenever the interface is re-configured, which might change the sentinel IPs
- When exiting gracefully, we delete the rule to restore normal DNS behavior without having to back up and restore the other IPs
- We also delete the rule at startup so that if Firezone crashes or misbehaves, restarting it should restore normal DNS
- We also flush the system-wide DNS cache whenever we claim different routes. This may flush too often, and it may also miss some flushes that we should do. It needs double-checking.
- There is still a gap when changing networks, DNS can leak there, but I don't think it's worse than before.
